claims.statement: Child sessions are full independent sessions (their own SessionDO, sandbox, and prompt queue) spawned by an agent acting in a parent session; the child inherits the parent's repository and identity but not its conversation history, and continues running after the parent responds.

Children can only be spawned while a prompt is processing: GET /internal/spawn-context resolves the prompt author from messageRepository.getProcessingMessageAuthor() and returns 400 'No active prompt found. Child operations must be triggered by an active prompt.' when there is none, so idle sessions and clients cannot spawn children.

POST /sessions/:id/children (handleSpawnChild) is the single agent-spawn choke point: it validates the body, checks the parent spawn depth (403), the lifetime total-children cap (429), fetches the parent's spawn context, pins the repository, resolves model/reasoning-effort against enabled models, copies provider auth, acquires a concurrent-capacity lease (429), initializes D1-first then the child DO, enqueues the initial prompt (failure marks the child failed, 500), and finally notifies the parent's DO.

Spawn depth is capped by MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH = 2 (403 when the parent's stored spawn_depth reaches it); getSpawnDepth is a single read of the sessions.spawn_depth column, and the child's depth is parentDepth + 1 persisted in both the D1 index and the DO session row.

Per-parent child caps come from the parent's resolved sandbox settings (global defaults layered with per-repo and per-environment overrides): default maxConcurrentChildSessions = 5 and maxTotalChildSessions = 15; countTotalChildren counts every row ever spawned under the parent (a lifetime count), and settings validation enforces maxConcurrentChildSessions <= maxTotalChildSessions.

Children are single-repo by design and pinned to the parent's scalar repository (the primary member of a multi-repo parent): an explicit repoOwner/repoName must match the parent exactly or spawn fails 403, a repo-less parent cannot gain repository context, and spawnContextSchema is deliberately scalar with no repositories array (cross-repo children are a named v1 non-feature, design §13.13).

The child model defaults to the parent's model and reasoning effort defaults to the parent's; a child override must be a valid model in the org's enabled set (else 400/503) and the reasoning effort must be valid for the selected model.

Children inherit the parent's complete provider-auth snapshot: each session_model_provider_auth row is copied with inheritedFromSessionId = parentId, agent child-spawn requests cannot override auth, and an unavailable or incomplete snapshot fails closed with 503 'Parent provider auth unavailable'.

Spawn preserves the create invariant that the D1 index row (lineage, provider auth, managed-skill manifest copy) is written before the child DO's /internal/init, so any D1 failure is caught before a sandbox spawns; if DO init fails the admission lease is released and the spawn returns 500 with nothing created.

After successful init, the spawn route enqueues the initial prompt to the child DO with source 'agent' and the processing prompt author's identity; if the enqueue throws or returns non-OK, the child row is immediately marked failed and the spawn returns 500.

Spawn returns 201 { sessionId, status: 'created' } before the child does any work and fire-and-forget posts /internal/child-session-update to the parent DO (background task session.notify_parent_spawn) so the parent's connected clients learn about the new child.

Every child status or title change notifies the parent DO: SessionStatusService.projectTransition and SessionTitleService call notifyParentOfChildUpdate, which background-fetches the parent's POST /internal/child-session-update; the parent's childSessionUpdate validates {childSessionId, status, title} and broadcasts a child_session_update event to the parent's WebSocket clients, and notification failures are logged, not thrown.

Concurrent capacity is enforced with lease tokens in the child_admission_leases table (lease_token PK, child_session_id UNIQUE, expires_at, FK to sessions ON DELETE CASCADE); acquireChildAdmissionLease atomically prunes expired leases and inserts only when live children plus unexpired leases are below maxConcurrentChildren, TTL is CHILD_ADMISSION_LEASE_TTL_MS = 5 minutes, finalizeChildAdmission deletes the lease when the child projects active, and releaseChildAdmissionLease deletes only the row matching the caller's lease token.

Resuming a terminal child (status completed or failed) is a new admission: handlePromptChild acquires a child admission lease before dispatch and releases it only when the child definitively rejects the prompt; on an ambiguous transport error the lease is deliberately retained (the child may have accepted the prompt before the response was lost) and capacity is restored by lease expiry or the child's active-state finalization.

Follow-up prompts (send-child-prompt) are queued, not interrupting: the router validates the body, verifies direct lineage in D1 (404), fetches the parent's token-free active-prompt-author, then the child DO re-verifies the child's stored parent_session_id matches (404 otherwise), checks isSessionPromptable (409 for cancelled/archived, promptability races map to 409, queue-full to 429), and enqueues with source 'agent' and SCM enrichment without tokens — the child's own stored SCM credentials are used for git operations; on success the router background-touches the child's updated_at.

The child read model (get-child-status with childId) proxies through the router (which verifies isChildOf) to the child DO's GET /internal/child-summary: ChildSummaryHandler builds a ChildSessionDetail with the scalar session mirror, sandbox status, parsed artifacts, the 5 most recent non-noisy events (token/heartbeat/step_start/step_finish filtered from a 50-row fetch), and hasUnfinishedPrompt from pending/processing counts; include=result projects the latest terminal message through buildAgentResponseFromEvents with event pages of 200 capped at 1000 and surfaces eventLimitReached; include=trajectory paginates the persisted event timeline (trajectoryLimit default 200, max 1000) via encodeEventTimelineCursor/parseEventTimelineCursor.

Cancellation cascades: POST /sessions/:id/children/:childId/cancel verifies direct lineage, cancels the child DO (tolerating 409 for terminal states), and unless cancelNested is false cancels live descendants returned by a recursive CTE that is depth-capped at MAX_DESCENDANT_DEPTH = 10, excludes inactive statuses (completed/failed/archived/cancelled), and orders bottom-up; non-conflict descendant failures aggregate into a 502 listing the children that could not be cancelled, while cancelling descendants of an already-terminal child is still reported as success.

Children routes authenticate with user-or-service-with-sandbox-fallback (spawn, list, get, cancel) or sandbox-only (prompt) policies binding :id as the parent session; the sandbox fallback verifies the bearer token against the parent DO's /internal/verify-sandbox-token, so the parent's sandbox token is never exchanged for the child's token, and authorization is two-layered: D1 lineage in the router plus the child DO's parent_session_id match.

The sandbox-side agent contract is four tools routing through the control-plane bridge (CONTROL_PLANE_URL + SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN, session id from SESSION_CONFIG): spawn-child requires an explicit affirmative user request to create a child session (not sub-agent/sub-task work, which uses the in-process Task tool) and returns the child id immediately; send-child-prompt queues follow-ups that run after current child work without interrupting (completed/failed children can resume, cancelled/archived cannot); get-child-status lists children or returns a formatted detail with include=result/trajectory support; cancel-child cancels with cancelNested defaulting to true.

Lineage is persisted on both the D1 row and the DO session row: parent_session_id, spawn_source ('agent' for spawned children), and spawn_depth; root_session_id is computed at D1 insert as the parent's root (or the session itself when it has no parent), and the child pins a copy of the parent's managed-skill manifest via managedSkillsSourceSessionId (SessionIndexStore.create rejects a session that both resolves and copies a manifest).

Children inherit their sandbox settings scope from the parent (repo + environment overrides) except sandboxTimeoutMs, which is taken from the spawn context (the parent's live sandbox timeout); the child starts from the parent's base branch (or DEFAULT_BASE_BRANCH), not the parent's working branch, and carries the environmentId, automationId, and automationRunId provenance of the parent.

Behavioral tests pin the critical invariants: router.spawn-child.test.ts asserts provider-auth copy with inheritedFromSessionId, reasoning-effort inheritance, fail-closed 503 on missing auth, and lease release on init failure; session-children.test.ts asserts the terminal-resume lease acquire/release/retain policy and cancel descendant aggregation; child-sessions.handler.test.ts asserts prompt-author attribution from the processing prompt author and the 404/409/429 rejection mapping; child-summary.handler.test.ts asserts noisy-event filtering and include gates.
